newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-DRUG SQUAD RAIDS MARADONA'S CLUB BOCA AND SOCCER BODY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DRUG SQUAD RAIDS MARADONA'S CLUB BOCA AND SOCCER BODY.

text.p: An Argentine police drug squad on Wednesday raided Diego Maradona's club Boca Juniors, the Argentina Football Association and a sports training centre where soccer match drug tests are examined.
Boca spokesman Ivan Pavlovsky told reporters at the Buenos Aires ground of Argentina's most famous club that police "asked for players' drug-test records and took them away."

He said they were interested in the records of tests done two months ago on Maradona -- who admits he takes drugs and was formerly banned for 15 months for failing a drugs test at the U.S. World Cup -- and Deportivo Espanol player Martin Vargas.
The test on Maradona, who recently spent 10 days at a Swiss drugs clinic, was negative. The test on Vargas was positive.

The test results caused an outcry in the sports press. Dr. Americo Ecuardo Ciarrochi, who is pushing a new drug law through Congress, asked in the sports newspaper El Grafico: "How can it be that Vargas's test is positive while that of Maradona, who recognises he is an addict, does not?"

Argentina Football Association Chairman Julio Grondona, taken by surprise by the raid, told reporters that police could "take whatever they want, from the basement to the top floor where the caretaker lives."
